answer: Autonomous agents trading saffron and violet crops resist Sybil attacks using flow-based trust networks. Each agent acts as a vertex whose operational capacity is bounded by flow routed from trusted seeds. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of acquiring authentic inbound trust edges from honest peers, because colluding subgraphs cannot widen the honest-to-adversarial cut. However, this model severely restricts newly deployed agents that lack established counterparties.
